note: Spike #115: design seven `srmech.spectral.*` ToolEntry specifications for next-rc registration (alongside Phase C1 in 0.4.0rcN+1 per user scope decision 2026-05-18). Design-only spike; no .py implementation driver. Tool-schema describes ALGEBRA per [[user_stance_framework_domain_algebra_not_length_or_magnitude]]; substrate-coupling magnitudes (D, k, sparsity threshold, predictor function) are inputs not framework operations. Identity-not-implementation discipline per [[user_stance_identity_not_implementation_discipline]]: each entry IS a Class A-N composition, it does not implement spectral analysis as a new primitive class. Composition layer one level above `srmech.amsc.*`.

name: SpectralHandle

fields.substrate_descriptor_path: str (relative to attested-root; the substrate-coupling SSoT)
fields.substrate_descriptor_hash: str (64-hex; Class A SHA-256 of canonical descriptor bytes per AMSC discipline)
fields.coefficients_bytes: bytes (BSC-encoded coefficient vector; D-bit / D-byte hypervector per Class M canon)
fields.content_sha: str (64-hex; Class A SHA-256 of coefficients_bytes for substrate-mismatch detection on delta)

rationale: Substrate-descriptor + content-SHA-keyed eigenbasis cache per Spike #112 scoping; substrate-coupling-isolated per [[user_stance_framework_domain_algebra_not_length_or_magnitude]]. Frozen dataclass; matches MPR-v1 attestation pattern (descriptor-bytes -> SHA-256 -> hash key). Eigenbasis cache is keyed by descriptor+kind, NOT by per-state content (eigenbasis is one-time substrate work; coefficients are per-state cheap work). Content_sha exists per-handle for delta-time substrate-mismatch detection (raise on mismatch).

eigenbasis_cache: keyed by (substrate_descriptor_hash, laplacian_kind); module-level LRU bounded to N_MAX_EIGENBASES (default 8); on miss, compute Class L hermitian_eigendecompose and cache
coefficient_cache: none — coefficients are per-state O(n) work and cheap to recompute
cache_invalidation: explicit srmech.spectral.clear_eigenbasis_cache() helper for test isolation; LRU eviction when N_MAX_EIGENBASES exceeded
persistent_cache: out of scope for v0.4.x; eigenbasis-as-MPR-attested artefact is future work (would let consumers ship pre-computed eigenbasis NDJSON files alongside descriptor)
rationale: Cost asymmetry: eigenbasis is O(n^3) one-time; coefficient decompose is O(n^2) per state; delta is O(D) per pair (Class M XOR). Match cache lifetime to cost class.

exceptions.SubstrateMismatchError: raised by delta/similarity when handle_a.substrate_descriptor_hash != handle_b.substrate_descriptor_hash (Class A SHA-256 mismatch on canonical descriptor bytes; substrate algebra cannot be compared across substrates)
exceptions.UnsupportedSubstrateError: raised by decompose when substrate_descriptor names a Laplacian kind unknown to Class L (e.g. fractional-Laplacian which is Spike #119+ scope)
exceptions.EncoderFailureError: raised by decompose when substrate-specific encoder fails (e.g. state shape mismatches descriptor.n_nodes)
exceptions.DimensionMismatchError: raised by delta when ref_coeffs and current_coeffs differ in length (Class M precondition)
exceptions.EmptyHistoryError: raised by predict when handle_history is empty (Class C cascade needs >=1 sample)

base_class: srmech.spectral.SpectralError (subclass of ValueError, mirroring srmech.amsc.hdc and srmech.amsc.laplacian convention)

discipline: Every Class A-N primitive earns a C surface per [[feedback_no_binding_layer_carveout]]. `srmech.spectral.*` is a COMPOSITION layer above primitives, NOT a new primitive class itself, so the `srmech.spectral.*` entries themselves are Python wrappers that compose existing libsrmech symbols.

per_entry_split.decompose: Python composition; calls libsrmech Class L hermitian_eigendecompose + substrate-specific encoder; encoder is Python (substrate-specific, not primitive)
per_entry_split.delta: Python composition; calls libsrmech Class M srmech_hdc_bind directly on coefficient bytes (Option B from Spike #114 — bind already C-shipped)
per_entry_split.recompose: Python composition; calls libsrmech Class L dense_matvec_complex + substrate-specific decoder; decoder is Python
per_entry_split.predict: Python composition; will call libsrmech Class L row-select + Class C cascade_extrapolate (Spike #113 scope, NEW Class C sub-op in libsrmech)
per_entry_split.prediction_error: Python composition; calls Class M bind + Class K gate (new Class K sub-op `gate_by_threshold` may be needed; Spike #117/#118 scope)
per_entry_split.truncate_sparse: Python composition; calls Class K `sparse_truncate` sub-op (NEW; Spike #117 scope)
per_entry_split.similarity: Python composition; calls libsrmech Class M srmech_hdc_similarity directly on coefficient bytes

verdict: Spike #115 itself adds ZERO new C primitives; ships the namespace + 7 ToolEntry registrations; relies on Spike #113 + #114 + #117 deliverables for full functionality. Spec-only ship for entries 4/5/6 is acceptable per RC-stacking discipline if their underlying Class C/K sub-ops are not yet C-shipped — entry summaries note 'requires spike #N completion' until ready.

name: srmech.spectral.decompose
signature: decompose(state: bytes | np.ndarray, substrate: SpectralSubstrate) -> SpectralHandle
summary: Decompose a substrate state into spectral coefficients via Class L eigenbasis projection. Substrate descriptor + Laplacian kind determine the eigenbasis (cached by content-SHA per Spike #112). Returns SpectralHandle for downstream delta / recompose / similarity.
canonical_ssot: Chung (1997) Spectral Graph Theory §1-2 (graph Laplacian eigendecomposition); Golub & Van Loan (1996) Matrix Computations §8.5 (Jacobi); chess-spectral §5 (substrate-as-graph framing)
ssot_verification: Chung 1997 cite-by-ref (textbook); Golub & Van Loan cite-by-ref (textbook); chess-spectral §5 in-repo at docs/chess-maths/chess_spectral_research_notebook.md (verifiable)
class_chain: L (eigenbasis) + A (descriptor hash for eigenbasis cache key)
substrate_coupling: substrate.laplacian_kind (combinatorial / normalised / signed-Laplacian-variant per Class L sub-op)
test_plan_stub: (a) bit-exact roundtrip decompose -> recompose on 4 substrates (chess / image / ephemeris / gear-DAG) at 9.29e-17 machine-zero tolerance per chess-spectral §5b; (b) eigenbasis-cache hit/miss verification (two decompose calls on same substrate; second is cache-hit, observable by zero hermitian_eigendecompose call); (c) substrate-coupling test (same state encoded under two different Laplacian kinds produces two different SpectralHandles)

name: srmech.spectral.delta
summary: Compute bit-exact delta between two encoded spectral coefficient vectors via Class M HDC bind (XOR). Option B surface per Spike #114: directly on already-encoded bytes, no re-encoding (1.22x speedup vs Option A wrapper, identity-not-implementation aligned).
canonical_ssot: Plate (1995) Holographic Reduced Representations §3.2 (binding self-inversion); Kanerva (2009) Hyperdimensional Computing §3.2 (BSC binding properties); chess-spectral §5b (rank-k delta identity)
ssot_verification: Plate 1995 IEEE TNN paywall cite-by-ref (verified citation in srmech.amsc.hdc docstring); Kanerva 2009 Cogn Comput paywall cite-by-ref (verified citation in srmech.amsc.hdc docstring); chess-spectral §5b in-repo (verifiable)
substrate_coupling: hypervector_dimension_D (preserved across both inputs; mismatch raises DimensionMismatchError)
test_plan_stub: bit-exact 4/4 substrates per Spike #114 (chess D=768, image D=4096, ephemeris D=384, gear-DAG D=96); self-inversion roundtrip bind(a, bind(a, b)) == b across substrates; commutativity bind(a, b) == bind(b, a); native-path parity vs Python fallback

name: srmech.spectral.recompose
signature: recompose(handle: SpectralHandle, deltas: Sequence[bytes] = ()) -> bytes | np.ndarray
summary: Reconstruct substrate state from a SpectralHandle, optionally applying a sequence of bind-deltas (each XORed onto the handle's coefficients in sequence) before decode. Inverse of decompose; chess-spectral §5b verified machine-zero (9.29e-17) on rank-1 path.
canonical_ssot: Chung (1997) Spectral Graph Theory §1-2 (inverse projection f = U c); chess-spectral §5b (verified machine-zero roundtrip)
class_chain: M (bind to apply deltas) + L (dense_matvec_complex for U @ c)
test_plan_stub: (a) recompose(decompose(state, s)) == state at machine-zero tolerance (9.29e-17 per chess-spectral §5b) on 4 substrates; (b) delta-chain composition: recompose(handle, [d1, d2]) == recompose(handle_after_d1d2) where handle_after_d1d2 is the handle whose coefficients have been bind-composed with d1 then d2; (c) empty-deltas case (deltas=()) returns same state as recompose(handle)

name: srmech.spectral.predict
signature: predict(handle_history: Sequence[SpectralHandle], predictor: Callable[[Sequence[bytes]], bytes] | str = 'cascade_extrapolate') -> SpectralHandle
summary: Generate a predicted next-state SpectralHandle by extrapolating from a coefficient history. Default predictor is Class C cascade_extrapolate (Rao-Ballard 1999 predictive coding; Friston 2010 free-energy framing). Predictor is a substrate-coupling input — user supplies their own callable for non-default predictors. NOTE: requires Spike #113 Class C cascade_extrapolate C sub-op shipping.
canonical_ssot: Rao & Ballard (1999) Nat Neurosci 2(1):79-87 predictive coding in cortex; Friston (2010) Nat Rev Neurosci 11(2):127-138 free-energy framework
ssot_verification: Rao-Ballard 1999 cite-by-ref (paywall; will verify PDF on next research-followup); Friston 2010 cited in srmech spike_46_round1_references.ndjson (verified prior)
class_chain: C (cascade_extrapolate) + L (eigenbasis preserved from history[-1] handle)
substrate_coupling: predictor function (Callable user-supplied or named-string built-in)
test_plan_stub: (a) trivial-predictor identity: predict([h], lambda hs: hs[-1]) returns handle with same coefficients as h; (b) cascade-extrapolate on circular-orbit ephemeris (predict step k+1 from steps [k-3..k]; verify rank-1 sparsity prediction-error per Spike #112 chess-spectral §5b identity); (c) substrate-mismatch on history with mixed substrates raises SubstrateMismatchError; (d) empty history raises EmptyHistoryError

name: srmech.spectral.prediction_error
signature: prediction_error(observed: SpectralHandle, predicted: SpectralHandle, threshold: float = 0.0) -> bytes
summary: Compute spectral prediction error as Class M bind(observed.coefficients, predicted.coefficients), optionally gated by Class K threshold (returns zero-vector when total weight below threshold; Lisman-Grace 2005 hippocampal novelty-filter analog). Sparser than naive delta when predictor is accurate (Rao-Ballard 1999).
canonical_ssot: Rao & Ballard (1999) Nat Neurosci 2(1):79-87 (error spectrum); Lisman & Grace (2005) Neuron 46(5):703-713 (hippocampal novelty gate); Friston (2010) Nat Rev Neurosci 11(2):127-138 (variational free energy)
ssot_verification: Rao-Ballard 1999 cite-by-ref paywall; Lisman-Grace 2005 cite-by-ref paywall (will verify PDF on next research-followup); Friston 2010 verified prior
class_chain: M (bind) + K (gate_by_threshold; Spike #117/#118 scope; may dissolve as Class K sub-op or stay as raw threshold compare)
substrate_coupling: substrate descriptor (both handles must match; SubstrateMismatchError on disagreement)
test_plan_stub: (a) perfect-prediction case: predict(history, perfect_predictor) -> prediction_error returns all-zero bytes; (b) one-bit-error: corrupt one bit of observed; prediction_error has hamming weight 1; (c) below-threshold gating: error with total hamming weight < threshold_bits returns zero-vector; (d) substrate-mismatch raises SubstrateMismatchError

name: srmech.spectral.truncate_sparse
signature: truncate_sparse(handle: SpectralHandle, k_or_threshold: int | float) -> SpectralHandle
summary: Class K asymptotic-DOF compression: keep top-k coefficients by magnitude (int input) or coefficients with |c_i| >= threshold (float input). Olshausen-Field 1996 sparse-coding analog. Lossy compression with bounded reconstruction error per Class K asymptotic-DOF rule. NOTE: requires Spike #117 Class K sparse_truncate C sub-op shipping.
canonical_ssot: Olshausen & Field (1996) Nature 381(6583):607-609 (sparse coding in V1)
ssot_verification: Olshausen-Field 1996 cite-by-ref paywall (will verify PDF on Spike #117 implementation)
class_chain: K (sparse_truncate; new Class K sub-op per Spike #117)
substrate_coupling: k (int; number of coefficients to keep) OR threshold (float; magnitude floor)
test_plan_stub: (a) k=D returns same handle (no-op when k equals full dimension); (b) k=0 returns zero-coefficient handle; (c) top-k preserves the k largest-magnitude coefficients (verify by argmax-set equality); (d) reconstruction-error bound: |recompose(truncate(h, k)) - recompose(h)| <= sum of dropped |c_i|^2 (Parseval identity verification at machine precision)

name: srmech.spectral.similarity
summary: HDC similarity between two SpectralHandles' coefficient vectors via Class M: 1 - 2 * hamming(a, b) / D, range [-1, +1]. +1 identical; 0 orthogonal; -1 complementary. Substrate-mismatch raises (handles must share substrate descriptor).
canonical_ssot: Kanerva (2009) Hyperdimensional Computing §3.2 (HDC similarity for BSC); Plate (1995) Holographic Reduced Representations §3.2
ssot_verification: Kanerva 2009 cite-by-ref (verified citation in srmech.amsc.hdc docstring); Plate 1995 cite-by-ref (verified citation in srmech.amsc.hdc docstring)
substrate_coupling: D_bits (both handles must match; DimensionMismatchError on disagreement)
substrate descriptor (both must match; SubstrateMismatchError on disagreement)
test_plan_stub: (a) similarity(h, h) == +1.0 (self-identity); (b) similarity(h, complement(h)) == -1.0 where complement flips every bit; (c) random pair on large D approaches 0.0 (orthogonality at D=1024 within +/- 3 sigma); (d) substrate-mismatch raises SubstrateMismatchError; (e) native-path parity vs Python fallback
